# Factory & Instance Registration

## Factory Method

Register a service using a factory method:

```csharp
[IocRegister<IMyService>(Factory = nameof(MyServiceFactory.Create))]
internal class MyService : IMyService;

public static class MyServiceFactory
{
    // Must be static
    public static IMyService Create()
    {
        return new MyService();
    }
}
```

<details>
<summary>Generated Code</summary>

```csharp
// <auto-generated/>
services.AddTransient<global::MyNamespace.MyService>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => (global::MyNamespace.MyService)global::MyNamespace.MyServiceFactory.Create());
services.AddTransient<global::MyNamespace.IMyService>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => sp.GetRequiredService<global::MyNamespace.MyService>());
```

</details>

The factory is called only by the implementation type's registration. Service types forward to it, so resolving `MyService` and `IMyService` gives the same instance for a singleton or scoped service. `Decorators` wrap that instance, as they do for constructor-created services. Generic factories (see [Generic Factory](#generic-factory)) are called separately for each service type.

A `Factory` given as a constant string instead of `nameof()`, such as a `const string`, is used as the method path and called with the `IServiceProvider` only, since its parameters are unknown.

### Factory of an Open Generic Type

On an open generic registration, the factory can use the implementation's type parameters. Each closed type used at compile time calls the factory of that closed type, and its parameters are resolved with the closed types:

```csharp
[IocRegister(ServiceLifetime.Singleton, ServiceTypes = [typeof(INode<>)], Factory = nameof(Create))]
public sealed class Node<T>(IRepo<T> repo) : INode<T>
{
    public static Node<T> Create(IRepo<T> repo) => new(repo);
}

// A dependency on INode<string> calls Node<string>.Create, resolving IRepo<string>
```

<details>
<summary>Generated Code</summary>

```csharp
// <auto-generated/>
// No open registration: Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection would construct Node<T> without the factory
services.AddSingleton<global::MyNamespace.Node<string>>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) =>
{
    var f_p0 = sp.GetRequiredService<global::MyNamespace.IRepo<string>>();
    return global::MyNamespace.Node<string>.Create(f_p0);
});
services.AddSingleton<global::MyNamespace.INode<string>>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => sp.GetRequiredService<global::MyNamespace.Node<string>>());
```

</details>

The factory can also be a member of another generic type, such as `Factory = nameof(Factories<T>.Create)`, which calls `Factories<string>.Create` for `Node<string>`.

> [!WARNING]
> No open registration (`typeof(Node<>)`) is added, because Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection would construct the type without the factory. Only the closed types used at compile time are registered, so a closed type that is only requested at runtime, such as `sp.GetService<INode<int>>()` with no `INode<int>` dependency, cannot be resolved (`SGIOC042`). Use the closed type in a dependency, register it, or discover it with `[IocDiscover<INode<int>>]` (see [Open Generics](09_OpenGeneric.md)).
>
> Earlier versions added the open registration, so such a type was constructed without the factory.

> [!WARNING]
> `nameof()` of an unbound generic type other than the implementation type, such as `Factory = nameof(Factories<>.Create)`, has no type arguments to close, so the registration is ignored (`SGIOC041`). Give the type arguments instead: `nameof(Factories<int>.Create)`, or `nameof(Factories<T>.Create)` on `Node<T>`. The same applies to `Instance` and to a `KeyType.Csharp` key.

### Factory Returning Different Implementations

> [!WARNING]
> The implementation type's registration casts the factory result to the implementation type, and service types resolve through it. A factory that returns another type, for example `new OtherService()` in the factory of `MyService`, throws `InvalidCastException` at resolution.

When the factory decides which implementation to create, register the factory for the service type itself. `IocRegisterFor<IMyService>` makes `IMyService` both the registered type and the target type, so the result is not cast to any implementation:

```csharp
[IocRegisterFor<IMyService>(ServiceLifetime.Singleton, Factory = nameof(MyServiceFactory.Create))]
public static class MyServiceFactory
{
    public static IMyService Create(IServiceProvider sp) =>
        Environment.ProcessorCount > 1 ? new FastService() : new SafeService();
}
```

<details>
<summary>Generated Code</summary>

```csharp
// <auto-generated/>
services.AddSingleton<global::MyNamespace.IMyService>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => global::MyNamespace.MyServiceFactory.Create(sp));
```

</details>

`FastService` and `SafeService` are not registered, so they cannot be resolved by their own types. Register them separately if consumers need them.

### Factory with Service Injection

Factory methods support **service injection just like constructors**. Any parameter that is not `IServiceProvider` or `[ServiceKey]` is automatically resolved from the DI container:

```csharp
[IocRegister<IMyService>(Factory = nameof(MyServiceFactory.Create))]
internal class MyService : IMyService;

public static class MyServiceFactory
{
    public static IMyService Create(IServiceProvider sp, ILogger logger)
    {
        return new MyService(logger);
    }
}
```

<details>
<summary>Generated Code</summary>

```csharp
// <auto-generated/>
services.AddTransient<global::MyNamespace.MyService>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) =>
{
    var f_p0 = sp.GetRequiredService<global::MyNamespace.ILogger>();
    return (global::MyNamespace.MyService)global::MyNamespace.MyServiceFactory.Create(sp, f_p0);
});
services.AddTransient<global::MyNamespace.IMyService>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => sp.GetRequiredService<global::MyNamespace.MyService>());
```

</details>

The following parameter kinds are supported:

|Parameter Kind|Example|Resolution|
|:---|:---|:---|
|`IServiceProvider`|`IServiceProvider sp`|Passed directly as `sp`|
|`[ServiceKey]`|`[ServiceKey] string key`|Passed as the registration key value, or `default!` when the registration has no key|
|Required service|`ILogger logger`|`sp.GetRequiredService<ILogger>()`|
|Optional service (nullable)|`ILogger? logger`|`sp.GetService<ILogger>() ?? default`|
|Default value|`int retries = 3`|`sp.GetService(typeof(int)) switch { int service => service, _ => 3 }` (the parameter's own default; also compiles for value types)|
|Default `null` on a non-nullable type|`ILogger logger = null`|`sp.GetService(typeof(ILogger)) switch { ILogger service => service, _ => default(ILogger)! }`|
|Keyed service|`[FromKeyedServices("key")] IConfig cfg`|`sp.GetRequiredKeyedService<IConfig>("key")`|
|Collection|`IEnumerable<IHandler> handlers`|`sp.GetServices<IHandler>()`|

### Mixed Parameters Example

A factory method can combine all parameter kinds:

```csharp
[IocRegister<IMyService>(
    ServiceLifetime.Scoped,
    Factory = nameof(MyServiceFactory.Create),
    Key = "myKey")]
internal class MyService : IMyService;

public static class MyServiceFactory
{
    public static IMyService Create(
        IServiceProvider sp,
        [ServiceKey] string key,
        ILogger logger,
        [FromKeyedServices("config")] IConfiguration config)
        => new MyService();
}
```

<details>
<summary>Generated Code</summary>

```csharp
// <auto-generated/>
services.AddKeyedScoped<global::MyNamespace.MyService>("myKey", (global::System.IServiceProvider sp, object? key) =>
{
    var f_p0 = sp.GetRequiredService<global::MyNamespace.ILogger>();
    var f_p1 = sp.GetRequiredKeyedService<global::MyNamespace.IConfiguration>("config");
    return (global::MyNamespace.MyService)global::MyNamespace.MyServiceFactory.Create(sp, "myKey", f_p0, f_p1);
});
services.AddKeyedScoped<global::MyNamespace.IMyService>("myKey", (global::System.IServiceProvider sp, object? key) => sp.GetRequiredKeyedService<global::MyNamespace.MyService>(key));
```

</details>

## Static Instance

Register a static instance (only allows `Singleton` lifetime):

```csharp
[IocRegister<IMyService>(ServiceLifetime.Singleton, Instance = nameof(Default))]
internal class MyService : IMyService
{
    public static readonly MyService Default = new();
}
```

<details>
<summary>Generated Code</summary>

```csharp
// <auto-generated/>
services.AddSingleton<global::MyNamespace.MyService>(global::MyNamespace.MyService.Default);
services.AddSingleton<global::MyNamespace.IMyService>(global::MyNamespace.MyService.Default);
```

</details>

An open generic type can provide its instance too. Each closed type used at compile time reads the instance of that closed type. No open registration is added, because Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection would construct the type instead of using the instance:

```csharp
[IocRegister(ServiceLifetime.Singleton, ServiceTypes = [typeof(INode<>)], Instance = nameof(Default))]
public sealed class Node<T> : INode<T>
{
    public static readonly Node<T> Default = new();
}

// A dependency on INode<string> registers Node<string>.Default
```

The instance can also be a member of another generic type that uses the implementation's type parameters, such as `Instance = nameof(Holder<T>.Default)`, which reads `Holder<string>.Default` for `Node<string>`. With `IocRegisterFor(typeof(Node<>))`, use the unbound form `Instance = nameof(Node<>.Default)`: a closed form such as `nameof(Node<int>.Default)` reads `Node<int>.Default` for every closed type.

### Instance with Keyed Service

```csharp
[IocRegister<IMyService>(ServiceLifetime.Singleton, Instance = nameof(Default), Key = "myKey")]
internal class MyService : IMyService
{
    public static readonly MyService Default = new();
}
```

<details>
<summary>Generated Code</summary>

```csharp
// <auto-generated/>
services.AddKeyedSingleton<global::MyNamespace.MyService>("myKey", global::MyNamespace.MyService.Default);
services.AddKeyedSingleton<global::MyNamespace.IMyService>("myKey", global::MyNamespace.MyService.Default);
```

</details>

> [!NOTE]  
> When using `Instance`, only `Singleton` lifetime is allowed. Using `Scoped` or `Transient` will not generate any registration code in the Register (`IServiceCollection`) output. A registration without `Lifetime` takes the lifetime of its matching [default settings](03_Defaults.md), otherwise the [`SourceGenIocDefaultLifetime`](13_MSBuild_Configuration.md) property (`Transient` when unset).

## Factory in Default Settings

You can specify a `Factory` in `IocRegisterDefaults` to apply it as the default factory for all services implementing the target type. Explicit `Factory` or `Instance` specified in `IocRegister` takes precedence over the default. With an `Instance`, no `Factory` is called and no `Decorators` are applied.

> [!NOTE]
> The default factory applies to other types, so `nameof()` of a member of an unbound generic type, such as `Factory = nameof(Factories<>.Create)`, has no type arguments to close, and the default settings are ignored (`SGIOC041`), even when it is the target type's own, such as `nameof(Node<>.Create)` for `IocRegisterDefaults(typeof(Node<>))`. Use a non-generic type or give the type arguments; to call the open generic type's own factory, register it with `[IocRegisterFor(typeof(Node<>), Factory = nameof(Node<>.Create))]` instead.

```csharp
[assembly: IocRegisterDefaults(
    typeof(IRepository<>),
    ServiceLifetime.Scoped,
    Factory = nameof(RepositoryFactory.Create))]

public interface IRepository<T> { T Get(int id); }

public static class RepositoryFactory
{
    public static object Create(IServiceProvider sp)
    {
        // Custom creation logic for all repositories
        return sp.GetRequiredService<object>();
    }
}

// Uses Factory from DefaultSettings
[IocRegister(ServiceTypes = [typeof(IRepository<>)])]
public class Repository<T> : IRepository<T>
{
    public T Get(int id) => default!;
}

// Entity for closed generic discovery
public class Customer { }

// This triggers closed generic registration with Factory
[IocRegister]
public class CustomerService(IRepository<Customer> repository);
```

<details>
<summary>Generated Code</summary>

```csharp
// <auto-generated/>
// No open registration: Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection would construct Repository<T> without the factory (SGIOC042)

// CustomerService registration
services.AddTransient<global::TestNamespace.CustomerService, global::TestNamespace.CustomerService>();

// Closed generic uses Factory from DefaultSettings
services.AddScoped<global::TestNamespace.Repository<global::TestNamespace.Customer>>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => (global::TestNamespace.Repository<global::TestNamespace.Customer>)global::TestNamespace.RepositoryFactory.Create(sp));
services.AddScoped<global::TestNamespace.IRepository<global::TestNamespace.Customer>>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => sp.GetRequiredService<global::TestNamespace.Repository<global::TestNamespace.Customer>>());
```

</details>

### Explicit Factory Overrides Default

When a registration specifies its own `Factory`, it overrides the default from `IocRegisterDefaults`:

```csharp
[assembly: IocRegisterDefaults(
    typeof(IHandler),
    ServiceLifetime.Scoped,
    Factory = nameof(DefaultFactory.Create))]

public interface IHandler { void Handle(); }

public static class DefaultFactory
{
    public static IHandler Create(IServiceProvider sp) => sp.GetRequiredService<DefaultHandler>();
}

public static class SpecialFactory
{
    public static IHandler Create(IServiceProvider sp) => new SpecialHandler();
}

// Uses Factory from DefaultSettings
[IocRegister(ServiceTypes = [typeof(IHandler)])]
public class DefaultHandler : IHandler
{
    public void Handle() { }
}

// Uses explicit Factory, overriding DefaultSettings
[IocRegister(ServiceTypes = [typeof(IHandler)], Factory = nameof(SpecialFactory.Create))]
public class SpecialHandler : IHandler
{
    public void Handle() { }
}
```

<details>
<summary>Generated Code</summary>

```csharp
// <auto-generated/>
// DefaultHandler uses Factory from DefaultSettings
services.AddScoped<global::TestNamespace.DefaultHandler>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => (global::TestNamespace.DefaultHandler)global::TestNamespace.DefaultFactory.Create(sp));
services.AddScoped<global::TestNamespace.IHandler>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => sp.GetRequiredService<global::TestNamespace.DefaultHandler>());

// SpecialHandler uses explicit Factory
services.AddScoped<global::TestNamespace.SpecialHandler>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => (global::TestNamespace.SpecialHandler)global::TestNamespace.SpecialFactory.Create(sp));
services.AddScoped<global::TestNamespace.IHandler>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => sp.GetRequiredService<global::TestNamespace.SpecialHandler>());
```

</details>

## Generic Factory

When working with open generic services, you can use a **generic factory method** to create instances. The generator needs to know how to map the service type's type parameters to the factory method's type parameters. There are two ways to specify this mapping:

1. **`[IocGenericFactory]`** on the factory method — use when you own the factory method.
2. **`GenericFactoryTypeMapping`** on the registration attribute — use when you cannot modify the factory (e.g., a third-party library).

Both use the same format:

- **First type**: The service type template with concrete placeholder types (e.g., `typeof(IRequestHandler<Task<int>>)`)
- **Remaining types**: The placeholder types that map to factory method type parameters in order

> [!WARNING]
> If `Factory` points to a generic method but neither `[IocGenericFactory]` nor a valid `GenericFactoryTypeMapping` is specified, analyzer `SGIOC016` is reported and registration will not be generated. The number of placeholder types must match the factory method's type parameter count, and each placeholder type must appear in the service type template.

> [!NOTE]
> When both `GenericFactoryTypeMapping` on the attribute and `[IocGenericFactory]` on the method are present, `[IocGenericFactory]` takes precedence.

### Using `[IocGenericFactory]`

Place the attribute on the factory method:

```csharp
[assembly: IocRegisterDefaults(
    typeof(IRequestHandler<>),
    ServiceLifetime.Singleton,
    Factory = nameof(FactoryContainer.Create))]

public interface IRequestHandler<TResponse> { }

public static class FactoryContainer
{
    // Map: IRequestHandler<Task<int>> placeholder 'int' -> type parameter T
    [IocGenericFactory(typeof(IRequestHandler<Task<int>>), typeof(int))]
    public static IRequestHandler<Task<T>> Create<T>() 
        => throw new NotImplementedException();
}

[IocRegister]
public class Handler<T> : IRequestHandler<Task<T>> { }

public class Entity { }

// Discover IRequestHandler<Task<Entity>>
[IocDiscover<IRequestHandler<Task<Entity>>>]
public sealed class App { }
```

<details>
<summary>Generated Code</summary>

```csharp
// <auto-generated/>
// Open generic registration
services.AddSingleton(typeof(global::TestNamespace.Handler<>), typeof(global::TestNamespace.Handler<>));

// Closed generic uses generic factory with Entity substituted for T
services.AddSingleton<global::TestNamespace.Handler<global::TestNamespace.Entity>, global::TestNamespace.Handler<global::TestNamespace.Entity>>();
services.AddKeyedSingleton<global::TestNamespace.IRequestHandler<global::System.Threading.Tasks.Task<global::TestNamespace.Entity>>>("SourceGen.Ioc.Decorated:TestNamespace.IRequestHandler<System.Threading.Tasks.Task<TestNamespace.Entity>>|TestNamespace.Handler<TestNamespace.Entity>", (global::System.IServiceProvider sp, object? key) =>
{
    var s0 = (global::TestNamespace.IRequestHandler<global::System.Threading.Tasks.Task<global::TestNamespace.Entity>>)global::TestNamespace.FactoryContainer.Create<global::TestNamespace.Entity>();
    return s0;
});
services.AddSingleton<global::TestNamespace.IRequestHandler<global::System.Threading.Tasks.Task<global::TestNamespace.Entity>>>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => sp.GetRequiredKeyedService<global::TestNamespace.IRequestHandler<global::System.Threading.Tasks.Task<global::TestNamespace.Entity>>>("SourceGen.Ioc.Decorated:TestNamespace.IRequestHandler<System.Threading.Tasks.Task<TestNamespace.Entity>>|TestNamespace.Handler<TestNamespace.Entity>"));
```

</details>

> [!NOTE]
> The factory method's parameters can use its type parameters. They are resolved with the type arguments the factory is called with: `Create<T>(IRepo<T> repo)` called as `Create<Entity>` resolves `IRepo<Entity>`, which closes an open generic `IRepo<>` registration.

> [!NOTE]
> A generic factory creates the instance of the service type it is closed for, so the factory result is not cast to the implementation type. Resolving the implementation type (`Handler<Entity>`) gives its own constructed instance. `Decorators` wrap the factory result, and `Lazy<T>` / `Func<T>` of the service type resolve the same instance through the hidden key.

> [!NOTE]
> The open registration of the implementation type (`typeof(Handler<>)`) is kept, since its closed types are constructed too. An open service type whose closed types call the factory, such as `typeof(IRequestHandler<>)` for `Handler<T> : IRequestHandler<T>` with the template `IRequestHandler<int>`, is not registered open, and neither is an implementation type that the template can match, such as `Handler<T>` for the template `Handler<int>` (`SGIOC042`, see [Factory of an Open Generic Type](#factory-of-an-open-generic-type)).

### Using `GenericFactoryTypeMapping`

Specify the mapping directly on the registration attribute. This is useful when you cannot modify the factory method (e.g., third-party code):

```csharp
// No [IocGenericFactory] attribute needed on the factory method
[assembly: IocRegisterDefaults(
    typeof(IRequestHandler<>),
    ServiceLifetime.Singleton,
    Factory = nameof(ExternalFactory.Create),
    GenericFactoryTypeMapping = [typeof(IRequestHandler<Task<int>>), typeof(int)])]

public static class ExternalFactory
{
    // Third-party or shared factory — cannot be modified
    public static IRequestHandler<Task<T>> Create<T>() 
        => throw new NotImplementedException();
}
```

`GenericFactoryTypeMapping` is available on `[IocRegisterDefaults]` and `[IocRegisterFor]`.

### How the Mapping Works

When a closed generic type is discovered (e.g., `IRequestHandler<Task<Entity>>`):

1. The generator compares it with the service type template (`IRequestHandler<Task<int>>`)
2. Extracts actual types from positions matching placeholder types (`int` → `Entity`)
3. Substitutes them into the factory method call: `Create<Entity>()`

Each placeholder type must appear in the template at least once, and may appear more than once. For `Create<T>()` with `[IocGenericFactory(typeof(IPair<int, int>), typeof(int))]`, `IPair<Entity, Entity>` calls `Create<Entity>()`, while `IPair<Entity, Dto>` gives `int` two different types, so it is not registered (`SGIOC039`).

A placeholder must be a type without type arguments that is not an array, such as `int`; `List<int>`, `int?`, `(int, string)` and `int[]` report `SGIOC016`. Placeholders can be array or tuple elements, though:

- `IFoo<int[]>` matches `IFoo<Entity[]>`, but not an array of another rank, such as `IFoo<Entity[,]>`.
- `IFoo<(int, string)>` matches `IFoo<(Entity, string)>`, with or without element names.

A placeholder that only appears in the type arguments of a containing type, such as `int` in `IFoo<Outer<int>.Inner>`, is not supported (`SGIOC016`).

A closed registration with a generic factory (its own, or from default settings) works the same way:

- each registered type that matches the template calls the closed factory;
- the implementation type is constructed when it does not match the template;
- a service type that does not match, such as `IRequestHandler<Entity>` or `IDisposable` from `RegisterAllInterfaces`, is not registered (`SGIOC039`), because the factory cannot be called for it.

```csharp
// Registers IRequestHandler<Task<Entity>> with Create<Entity>() and EntityHandler with new EntityHandler()
[IocRegister(RegisterAllInterfaces = true, Factory = nameof(FactoryContainer.Create))]
internal sealed class EntityHandler : IRequestHandler<Task<Entity>>;
```

### Multiple Type Parameters

For services with multiple type parameters, use different placeholder types for each:

```csharp
[assembly: IocRegisterDefaults(
    typeof(IRequestHandler<,>),
    ServiceLifetime.Singleton,
    Factory = nameof(FactoryContainer.Create))]

public interface IRequestHandler<TRequest, TResponse> { }

public static class FactoryContainer
{
    // Map: 'int' -> T1, 'decimal' -> T2
    [IocGenericFactory(
        typeof(IRequestHandler<Task<int>, List<decimal>>), 
        typeof(int), 
        typeof(decimal))]
    public static IRequestHandler<Task<T1>, List<T2>> Create<T1, T2>() 
        => throw new NotImplementedException();
}

[IocRegister]
public class Handler<T1, T2> : IRequestHandler<Task<T1>, List<T2>> { }

public class Entity { }
public class Dto { }

// Discover IRequestHandler<Task<Entity>, List<Dto>>
[IocDiscover(typeof(IRequestHandler<Task<Entity>, List<Dto>>))]
public sealed class App { }
```

<details>
<summary>Generated Code</summary>

```csharp
// <auto-generated/>
// Open generic registration
services.AddSingleton(typeof(global::TestNamespace.Handler<,>), typeof(global::TestNamespace.Handler<,>));

// Closed generic with T1=Entity, T2=Dto
services.AddSingleton<global::TestNamespace.Handler<global::TestNamespace.Entity, global::TestNamespace.Dto>, global::TestNamespace.Handler<global::TestNamespace.Entity, global::TestNamespace.Dto>>();
services.AddKeyedSingleton<global::TestNamespace.IRequestHandler<global::System.Threading.Tasks.Task<global::TestNamespace.Entity>, global::System.Collections.Generic.List<global::TestNamespace.Dto>>>("SourceGen.Ioc.Decorated:TestNamespace.IRequestHandler<System.Threading.Tasks.Task<TestNamespace.Entity>, System.Collections.Generic.List<TestNamespace.Dto>>|TestNamespace.Handler<TestNamespace.Entity, TestNamespace.Dto>", (global::System.IServiceProvider sp, object? key) =>
{
    var s0 = (global::TestNamespace.IRequestHandler<global::System.Threading.Tasks.Task<global::TestNamespace.Entity>, global::System.Collections.Generic.List<global::TestNamespace.Dto>>)global::TestNamespace.FactoryContainer.Create<global::TestNamespace.Entity, global::TestNamespace.Dto>();
    return s0;
});
services.AddSingleton<global::TestNamespace.IRequestHandler<global::System.Threading.Tasks.Task<global::TestNamespace.Entity>, global::System.Collections.Generic.List<global::TestNamespace.Dto>>>((global::System.IServiceProvider sp) => sp.GetRequiredKeyedService<global::TestNamespace.IRequestHandler<global::System.Threading.Tasks.Task<global::TestNamespace.Entity>, global::System.Collections.Generic.List<global::TestNamespace.Dto>>>("SourceGen.Ioc.Decorated:TestNamespace.IRequestHandler<System.Threading.Tasks.Task<TestNamespace.Entity>, System.Collections.Generic.List<TestNamespace.Dto>>|TestNamespace.Handler<TestNamespace.Entity, TestNamespace.Dto>"));
```

</details>

### Reversed Type Parameter Mapping

The placeholder order determines the mapping. You can map placeholders to type parameters in any order:

```csharp
public static class FactoryContainer
{
    // First placeholder (decimal) -> T1, second placeholder (int) -> T2
    // This reverses the mapping!
    [IocGenericFactory(
        typeof(IRequestHandler<Task<int>, List<decimal>>), 
        typeof(decimal),  // -> T1 
        typeof(int))]     // -> T2
    public static IRequestHandler<Task<T2>, List<T1>> Create<T1, T2>() 
        => throw new NotImplementedException();
}
```

When discovering `IRequestHandler<Task<Entity>, List<Dto>>`:

- `Task<Entity>` matches `Task<int>` → `int` maps to `T2` → `T2 = Entity`
- `List<Dto>` matches `List<decimal>` → `decimal` maps to `T1` → `T1 = Dto`
- Result: `Create<Dto, Entity>()`

> [!WARNING]  
> **Placeholder types must be unique!** Using the same type for multiple placeholders (e.g., `typeof(int), typeof(int)`) will cause SGIOC017 error and no registration will be generated, because the generator cannot determine which actual type maps to which type parameter.

### Generic Factory with IServiceProvider

Generic factories can also receive `IServiceProvider`:

```csharp
public static class FactoryContainer
{
    [IocGenericFactory(typeof(IRequestHandler<Task<int>>), typeof(int))]
    public static IRequestHandler<Task<T>> Create<T>(IServiceProvider sp) 
    {
        var logger = sp.GetRequiredService<ILogger>();
        return new Handler<T>(logger);
    }
}
```

## Diagnostics

|ID|Severity|Description|
|:---|:---|:---|
|SGIOC008|Error|`Factory` or `Instance` uses `nameof()`, but the referenced field/property/method is not `static` or is inaccessible.|
|SGIOC009|Error|`Instance` is specified but the lifetime (the `Lifetime` of the attribute, otherwise of its default settings, otherwise `SourceGenIocDefaultLifetime`) is not `Singleton`.|
|SGIOC010|Error|Both `Factory` and `Instance` are specified on the same attribute. `Instance` takes precedence.|
|SGIOC016|Error|Generic factory method has no valid type parameter mapping: neither `[IocGenericFactory]` nor `GenericFactoryTypeMapping` is specified, the placeholder count does not match the factory method's type parameters, or a placeholder type does not appear in the service type template.|
|SGIOC017|Error|Placeholder types in `[IocGenericFactory]` or `GenericFactoryTypeMapping` are duplicated. Each placeholder type must be unique within its mapping.|
|SGIOC039|Warning|A service type of a registration with a generic factory does not match the service type template of the factory's mapping, so the factory cannot be called for it and it is not registered. An implementation type that does not match is constructed instead, unless it cannot be constructed (an interface, an abstract or static class, or a class without a public constructor or an internal one it can access: declared in the same assembly, or in an assembly that gives it access with `InternalsVisibleTo`), in which case it is not registered either.|
|SGIOC041|Error|`Factory`, `Instance` or a `KeyType.Csharp` `Key` uses `nameof()` of a member of an unbound generic type other than the implementation type, such as `nameof(Factories<>.Create)`. Its type arguments cannot be determined, so the registration is ignored. The `Factory` of `IocRegisterDefaults` cannot use any unbound generic type, as it applies to other types; such default settings are ignored.|
|SGIOC042|Warning|The closed types of an open generic registration call its `Factory` (its own or from default settings), so no open registration is added: Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection would construct the type without the factory. Only the closed types used at compile time are registered, and a closed type that is only requested at runtime cannot be resolved. Use it in a dependency, register it, or discover it with `[IocDiscover]`.|
